artboards.name: home-page
artboards.role: Marketing home page for a pizzeria ('Forno Rosso'): header, hero, delivery promo banner, featured menu grid, brand-story section, and footer with business info. Single screen at desktop width (1440); no other artboards or revisions are present on this canvas.

artboards.name: header
artboards.role: Sticky-style top navigation: brand logo, primary nav links, delivery estimate + cart button.

artboards.name: hero
artboards.role: Above-the-fold hero: eyebrow badge, two-tone headline, supporting copy, primary/secondary CTAs, hero product photo.

artboards.name: delivery-banner
artboards.role: Full-width promo strip: free-delivery message plus two stat callouts (ETA, temperature guarantee).

artboards.name: featured-section
artboards.role: Featured menu: section heading plus a 4-up grid of pizza cards with photo, name, price, description, and an add-to-order action.

artboards.name: story-section
artboards.role: Brand-story section: heading, paragraph, a 3-item feature/trust list with icons, and a two-photo image collage.

artboards.name: footer
artboards.role: Site footer carrying business information: brand recap + social links, kitchen hours, pizzeria location/contact, and a legal bottom bar. Primary scope of MT-STORY-042.

open_questions.topic: Hero badge icon looks mismatched to its label
open_questions.detail: The icon inside the 'Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired' badge (node 6:679, layer name 'fire-extinguisher') is literally drawn as a fire-extinguisher glyph, not a flame/fire icon one would expect next to 'woodfired' copy. This looks like an icon-library mis-pick rather than an intentional choice.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement literally as drawn (fire-extinguisher icon) since the PNG is authoritative for visuals; flagging so design can confirm intent before the icon asset is finalized.

open_questions.topic: No defined behavior for pizza names that overflow the title/price row
open_questions.detail: 'Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo' (node 6:77) and 'Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola' (node 6:101) both exceed the 262px-wide name+price row and are clipped with an ellipsis in the rendered PNG. The Figma text node itself holds the full untruncated string — the truncation is a rendering artifact of the fixed-width row, not a scripted state.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Apply CSS single-line truncation (text-overflow: ellipsis) to the card title so long names degrade the same way the PNG shows, rather than wrapping or growing the card header.

open_questions.topic: Pizza cards have inconsistent internal height
open_questions.detail: The 'Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola' card's description block is 157px tall (node 6:99) vs. 136px for the other three (e.g. 6:63), because its description text runs to 3 lines. All four outer cards are still sized 302x441 in Figma, meaning the reference file itself has a small unaddressed inconsistency (the taller card's content technically doesn't fit its own frame).
open_questions.arc_assumption: Let PizzaCard's height be intrinsic/auto (not a fixed 441px) so a 3-line description doesn't get clipped, and let the grid row size to the tallest card via CSS grid `align-items: stretch`.

open_questions.topic: No URLs given for social icons or footer legal links
open_questions.detail: Instagram/Facebook/Twitter icons (nodes 6:145, 6:147, 6:149) and the 'Privacy Policy' / 'Delivery Terms' footer links (nodes 6:174, 6:175) are static icons/text in Figma with no destination annotated.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Wire them as placeholder links (`href="#"` / config-driven) that the implementer or a follow-up story fills in with real URLs.

open_questions.topic: Frame is desktop-only (1440px); no tablet/mobile breakpoints in the design
open_questions.detail: Every artboard on this canvas is fixed at 1440 width; there is no companion mobile or tablet frame for the header, hero, featured grid, story section, or footer.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Build the standard responsive collapse (nav condensing, grid columns reducing, footer columns stacking) using ordinary breakpoint conventions, since none are specified; this is a detail for a human to confirm against brand/product expectations before sign-off.

open_questions.topic: Cart badge count is a static '3' in the design
open_questions.detail: The header cart button (node 6:22) shows a hardcoded badge value of '3' with no empty/zero state drawn.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treat the badge value as dynamic application state (e.g. cart item count), defaulting to hidden or '0' when empty, rather than a hardcoded '3'.
